named_confounds: sparse and imbalanced early sample (about 750 early vs 6000 late works)
date uncertainty (about half of works have low/medium date confidence)
origin mix (many works of unknown origin; US effect is smaller)
one passage per work, so each work rate is 0 or 1
rationale: 6766 works, each with exactly one passage; the rate is count__domains__DISTANCE_TRAVEL/n_passages. Early means year<1876 and late means year>=1876. All years are present. Within each genre I took the late-minus-early difference in mean work-level rates, then averaged those differences across the 8 genres with equal weight. Estimate: -0.050. 95% CI from a 2000-replicate bootstrap resampling works within each genre-period cell: [-0.080,-0.021]. All 8 genres show a decrease, ranging from -0.04 to -0.06. Sensitivity checks: high-date-confidence works only -0.062, single-edition works -0.049, UK -0.059, US -0.022 (smaller, and no CI computed). Decade means fall from about 0.12-0.20 before 1870 to about 0.09-0.11 after 1880. The decline seems to happen around the 1870s-1880s and then levels off, so this looks like a step change rather than a steady trend. Caveats: early cells are small (37-165 works per genre), dates are uncertain, the coding procedure may have changed over time, and the corpus is a sample whose composition may differ between periods. Cited passages are coded with this domain and only show what the construct looks like; they do not prove the trend.
